inspection_method: Read targeted HTML/CSS/source sections from Concepts/PMConcept.html.
Rendered the local file with installed Google Chrome through Playwright to inspect Home, Agent Config, and Settings states.

concept_status.summary: PMConcept.html is useful visual/concept evidence for GUI direction, but it is not final product UI and must not override canonical Plans or accepted ledger decisions.

relevant_gui_patterns.summary: The concept uses a persistent top navigation with Home, Projects, Planning Wizard, Orchestrator, Usage, Agent Config, and Settings.

Home/dashboard shows Orchestrator Status, Current Task, Platform Quota, and a System Health widget; this is useful as visual language for an ambient setup status card, but too dense for initial onboarding.
Agent Config includes provider status cards with Ready and Needs Setup states, plus an Effective Runtime inspector showing provider, model, auth family, account, provider source, and raw identity.

Detailed provider rows use compact state badges such as ready, needs-setup, logged-in, validating, auth-expired, disconnected, with actions like Refresh, Revalidate, Update Key, and billing entity selection.
Usage has a compact provider health strip summarizing 7 Ready, 1 Degraded, and 1 Unavailable across providers.

Settings includes a System group with Authentication & Accounts, Health & Doctor, and Permissions & Rules. The Health & Doctor card has All Systems Go and Run Doctor Now; the inspector view has Run Doctor Checks and check categories CLI Tools, Git, Runtimes, Browser Tools, Capabilities, and Project Setup.
The Planning Wizard has a Project Setup step and multi-step workflow, but this is a planning-flow pattern, not a complete app first-run onboarding path.
Settings includes an Interaction Mode (ELI5) toggle and search-based navigation, both useful patterns for a newbie-friendly setup path if simplified.

synthesis: PMConcept.html supports using compact cards, state badges, health strips, and inspector-style details for the Doctor/onboarding redesign.

The concept also confirms a likely overexposure problem: full shell, code panes, terminal panes, Settings grids, Effective Runtime internals, and detailed provider rows are too much for first-run vibecoder onboarding.
The redesign should borrow the concept's visual grammar without copying its density into first-run.

A good direction is a simple Home/setup entry point with a small readiness summary and one primary action, with Agent Config, Settings Health & Doctor, Usage provider health, and support diagnostics as drill-down destinations.
The concept's Project Setup wizard is a useful staged-flow pattern, but it should not be mistaken for app onboarding.
negative_constraints: Do not treat PMConcept.html as final GUI canon.
Do not make the dense Home/code/terminal/dashboard shell the required first-run experience for newbie vibecoders.
Do not expose Effective Runtime raw identity, requested/effective internals, provider source, auth family, account, quota details, or raw diagnostics in normal onboarding by default.
Do not turn Settings Health & Doctor into a hidden-only destination; onboarding should surface a simple check-my-setup entry before advanced details.
candidate_questions: Should first-run onboarding appear as a simplified Home setup card/banner that uses PMConcept visual language before the full shell, or as a modal/wizard outside the normal shell?

Which PMConcept surfaces should be the drill-down destinations from the simple setup summary: Agent Config, Settings Health & Doctor, Usage provider health, support diagnostics, or all of them with progressive disclosure?
non_actions: No Plans/.plan_index, WorkNodes, NodeSeeds, executable queues, Spec_Lock, shards, evidence, plan_graph, or auto_decisions were created or updated.
